rules.title: 📖 Rules (as taught in class)
rules.li1: Everyone gets an island base with a port and a starting fleet: 2 schooners and a frigate. The port earns a little gold every turn and 🏰 shoots back at whoever attacks it — you can't take a base with a single ship.
rules.li2: One turn — one action: buy ships, collect loot, move one ship "along the ruler" or fire. With the "Three ships per turn" option (set when creating the game) you get up to three actions per turn with different ships — faster and livelier.
rules.li3: ⛵ With "Three ships per turn" neighbouring ships can sail in convoy: mark a flagship and a couple of neighbours, and the whole formation moves in one gesture, for one manoeuvre (at the speed of the slowest, led by the most senior ship). A convoy can't be formed in contact with the enemy — no running away as a squadron.
rules.li4: A longboat sitting in a fishing spot earns gold every turn by itself — it costs no action. A treasure island can be looted by any ship that reaches it (the "Collect" button).
rules.li5: Sink a ship — loot the gold from its wreck. Destroy a port — that rival is out, and you take half of their treasury.
rules.li6: Neutral pirates 🏴‍☠️ roam the sea — they drift slowly between turns, may vanish into the fog and reappear. Sink a pirate for the bounty, and the fat 👑 boss pays a fortune!
rules.li7: The battleship 🛳 hits enemy ports 1.5× harder — the main siege ship, though even it needs several broadsides to bring a base down.
rules.li8: Any warship can fire a 💥 broadside — but only to the side (bow and stern can't reach): aim sideways and the whole flank covers every enemy ship in the sector at once. Strongest when the enemy is exactly abeam, weaker towards the edges and with distance. A lifesaver when a pack surrounds you. Fishing longboats have no broadside.
rules.li9: Rival taking forever? "📯 Hurry up" — and they get 10 minutes to move. Hopelessly stuck yourself — you can strike your colours 🏳️.

goal.p: Destroy a rival's port and they are out. The last port standing wins the battle. 👑

single.p: Players take turns. One turn — one action:

turn.liFire: 🔥 fire at a target with a ship;

multi.p: Players take turns. One turn — up to three actions. Moving and firing can be done with different ships (one ship — no more than once per turn):
multi.budget: Each of these spends one of the three actions. Finished early (1–2 ships is no reason to drag it out) — hit "✅ End turn".
multi.convoy: ⛵ Convoy — bring up reinforcements as a group instead of one by one. Tap a ship, pick ⛵ in the ring, mark the neighbouring ships (up to three including the flagship) and drag from the flagship — the whole formation sails, keeping its shape. The entire convoy costs one manoeuvre, so a squadron can cross half the map in a turn instead of three. The price for that speed: it moves at the pace of the slowest ship (a battleship in the convoy cuts everyone's range), and a convoy cannot be formed in battle — if an enemy ship or a pirate is within firing range, you can't escape as a squadron, move the ships one at a time. The flagship must be the senior ship: a longboat won't tow a frigate — lead with the bigger vessel. Bots use convoys just like you do.

wind.p: Every battle has wind — the compass in the top right corner of the map (the arrow shows where it blows, its length the strength). Downwind you sail further, upwind less (up to ±35%), which is why the movement range is a teardrop stretched along the wind. The wind changes between turns (during your own turn it holds steady — plan calmly): catch a tailwind for an attack and don't let yourself be pinned upwind.

rt.p1: A switch when creating the battle: a game without turns — everything happens at once and continuously, like in a real-time strategy. Click anywhere — the ship sails there by itself and steers around islands. Turning follows an arc: the heavier the ship, the slower it swings onto the other tack (a battleship takes about five seconds), so plan manoeuvres ahead. Broadsides and the mortar fire on cooldown (each side has its own), while port income and fishing tick with time.
rt.p2: Available in every mode (online and against the computer): in "Development" the peace period runs on a timer (a banner counts down above the map), in a duel you buy your fleet as usual. The ⏸ button in the header pauses the game — the whole world freezes (cooldowns, income, bots); any player can unpause. While in beta it is unranked.

move.p: Pick your ship and press "Sail". A range outline appears — place the ship anywhere inside it (not onto islands, and not right up against other ships). Every class has its own range, and 🌬 the wind stretches the outline: downwind you go further, upwind less.

broadside.p1: The main weapon of every warship and the best way to sink a fleet. Pick a ship, press "Broadside" and aim to the side — the whole flank hits every enemy in the sector at once (your own ships and fishing longboats are spared). Damage is highest when the enemy is exactly perpendicular to the middle of the side (there the broadside hits as hard as the ship's full shot) and weaker towards the edges of the sector; it also falls off with distance. So it pays to turn side-on and get close.
broadside.p2: Guns per side: schooner 2, brig 3, frigate and battleship 4. A broadside from one side is your action for the turn, and the other side of the same ship can fire immediately afterwards for free (just swing the aim the other way). When a target runs out of HP it sinks and you loot ≈50% of its price.

mortar.p: Only on the frigate and the battleship. An aimed single shot in any direction (including bow and stern, where a broadside can't reach). Against ships it hits at half strength — its job is not trading fire at sea but sieges: against an enemy port it hits at full strength (and the battleship ×1.5 on top). Want to sink a fleet — broadside; want to bring a base down — mortar. Per turn a ship does one thing: mortar, broadside or sail.

repairer.p1: A support ship: instead of firing it repairs the allied fleet. Select it, press "Repair" → tap your damaged ship inside the yellow radius (slightly less than its movement range) — it restores ≈15% of that ship's hull (a yellow beam). Per turn: either sail or repair one ship. Same size and speed as a brig, but it does not fight: keep it behind your warships.
repairer.p2: 🔧 Materials — the yellow bar under the HP bar: a repair ship can only patch up a limited number of times (one notch per repair, whatever the ship). Out of materials — go back to your base and press "Restock" (the button appears near the base, like "Collect").

econ.fish: 🐟 Fishing spots — a longboat sitting in a zone earns gold at the start of each of your turns (it costs no action). A spot feeds a limited number of boats: 4, and large zones 5. The blue counter under the zone (e.g. 2/4) shows taken/limit. Fish migrate very slowly — the shoal wanders around its spots, so watch it and move your longboats.
econ.loot: 🏝 Treasure islands — any ship that reaches an island loots the treasure.
econ.tribute: 🏴‍☠️ Jackpot — destroy a port and you take 100–1000 gold, the more the bigger the game the eliminated player had (earned, fought, sank).
econ.port: 🏰 Port income — a little gold at the start of each of your turns. The poorer your fleet, the more generous the port: with no ships at all it pays 2.5 times more, and the bonus fades away smoothly as your fleet grows to the price of a brig.

outpost.p1: Once you loot an island it becomes your foothold: bring a ship right up to it and press "⛺ Outpost". After that you don't need the ship: click your outpost and a panel opens with its perks and an "⬆ Upgrade" button. Perks work within a radius around the island, and income grows with the level:
outpost.lvl1: ⛺ Outpost (150) — a lookout: clears the fog around the island + 3 gold/turn.
outpost.lvl2: 🏪 Trading post (250) — 8 gold/turn + repairs your ships nearby (≈3% of their hull per turn).
outpost.lvl3: 🏰 Fort (400) — 12 gold/turn + a shore gun: it fires at enemies and pirates in range by itself.
outpost.p2: Someone else's outpost can only be destroyed by the 🎯 mortar (frigate/battleship): pick a ship → "Mortar" → tap the island. A destroyed island belongs to nobody again — build anew. During the peace period of "Development" other players' buildings can't be touched.

port.p: Your base with its port. The port is very tough (840 HP) and shoots back at whoever attacks it (dealing return damage, and the wreck is yours). A single light ship won't take a base; even a battleship (the main siege vessel, whose mortar hits a port 1.5× harder) needs several shots rather than a couple of pokes — and takes return fire all that time (the port hits a battleship 20% harder). It is more effective to press a base with several ships. Lose your port and you are out.

fleet.legend: ❤️ hull · ⚔️ damage · 🎯 firing range · 🧭 movement (in cells)

fog.p: If it was switched on when the game was created, the map is covered in fog. Rival bases show up dimly, but their HP and fate (standing/destroyed) only update once you scout the place. Enemy ships, treasure islands and fishing zones stay invisible until you come close. Your base and each of your ships clear the fog (a little beyond their own radius) — sink that ship and the gloom closes in again. Not available on a single device.

pirates.p: Neutral ships drift across the sea between turns, and may dissolve into the fog and reappear. Sink one for the bounty. Small pirates nip at everyone, fishing longboats included. Now and then a fat 👑 boss arrives with a big payout — and it is aggressive: spotting a damaged ship nearby, it moves in to finish the job regardless of return fire. Careful: pirates you hit shoot back during other players' turns.

tut.hello: ⚓ Ahoy, captain! A few short hints and off to battle. This is "sea battle on squared paper".
tut.port: This is your port and fleet. The port earns a little gold every turn and shoots back 🏰 at whoever attacks it. Lose the port and you are out — look after it!
tut.turnMulti: You take turns. One turn — up to three actions: move and fire with different ships (one ship once per turn), collect loot, buy at the shipyard. Done early — hit "✅ End turn".
tut.turnSingle: You take turns. One turn — only one action: sail, fire, collect loot or visit the shipyard.
tut.move: Tap your ship → "Sail" (within the outline; 🌬 downwind it stretches — you get further!) or "💥 Broadside". The main attack is the broadside: it only hits to the side (turn side-on to the enemy!) and you aim it like a move. The closer the target is to the side, the more it hurts.
tut.broadside: Each side fires once per turn, but you can fire both port and starboard (that is one action). And the frigate and battleship also have a 🎯 Mortar — an aimed shot at a single target, including a port (a siege).
tut.convoy: ⛵ Convoy: neighbouring ships can sail together for a single manoeuvre — so you don't herd reinforcements one by one. Tap a ship, press ⛵ in the ring, mark the neighbours (up to three) and drag from the flagship. The convoy moves at the pace of the slowest ship, must be led by the senior one, and cannot be formed in battle.
tut.shop: At the Shipyard you buy ships for gold 💰: quick schooners and brigs, powerful frigates, fishing longboats — and the battleship, which hits ports harder than anything 🏰.
tut.gold: This is your balance — gold 💰. Earn it by fishing, treasure and sinking enemies, and spend it at the Shipyard on new ships.
tut.fish: Put a longboat in this 🐟 fishing zone — it will earn gold every turn by itself, and it costs no action.
tut.loot: And this is a treasure island 💰 — bring any ship right up to it and press "Collect" to take the gold.
tut.outpost: ⛺ A looted island is already a foothold: bring a ship close → "⛺ Outpost". After that click the building and upgrade it: a 🏪 Trading post repairs ships nearby, a 🏰 Fort adds a shore gun and more gold. Other players' buildings can only be broken by the 🎯 mortar.
tut.pirates: Pirates 🏴‍☠️ roam the sea — sink them and take the bounty. And a fat 👑 boss carries a big payout! But careful: pirates shoot back. On top of gold they drop 🪙 coins: one for a regular pirate, two for a boss. Save them up — there will be something to spend them on.
tut.goal: The goal is to destroy your rival's port. Bring your fleet up and shell their base. Good luck, captain! 🏴‍☠️

barkas.name: Fishing longboat
barkas.desc: Sitting in a fishing spot it earns {{fishing}} gold every turn by itself, and it costs no action. Barely armed.

shkhuna.name: Schooner
shkhuna.desc: A quick and cheap workhorse. Fires a broadside (2 guns per side). Good for scouting and looting.

brig.name: Brig
brig.desc: A balanced warship. Broadside of 3 guns per side.

fregat.name: Frigate
fregat.desc: A heavy warship of the line: a 4-gun broadside + a 🎯 mortar (an aimed shot, ports included).

linkor.name: Battleship
linkor.desc: King of the sea: a 4-gun broadside + a 🎯 mortar that hits ports at 1.5× (≈98). Slow, but almost unsinkable.

repair.name: Repair ship
repair.desc: A repair vessel. Per turn it either sails or patches up ONE of your ships in range — restoring ≈15% of its hull (a yellow beam). The size and speed of a brig, but it does not fight — keep it covered.

carrier.name: Aircraft carrier
carrier.desc: A military carrier: a rapid burst of five shells, very tough and very fast. A test ship.

pirate.name: Pirate ship
pirate.desc: A neutral drifter. Sink it and take the bounty. But watch out — it can shoot back.

deathmatch.name: Deathmatch
deathmatch.desc: Lots of gold at the start — a big fleet and carnage right away. The bots are aggressive.

develop.name: Development
develop.desc: The first rounds are peaceful: build up your economy and defences, then war. Every base gets its own fishing zone.

duel.name: Duel
duel.desc: 1v1 (or against a bot). A small map with no bases or islands: spend everything on your fleet at the start and wreck your rival's. There is no income per turn — gold only from pirates.

battery.name: Coastal Battery
battery.desc: Your port hits back harder at attackers: 25 → 40 damage (20% more against a battleship).

market.name: Trade Row
market.desc: Your port income is one and a half times larger every turn.

drydock.name: Dry Dock
drydock.desc: Your ships near your base repair themselves — 5% of hull every turn.

lighthouse.name: Lighthouse
lighthouse.desc: You see much farther around your base — the fog pulls back.

garrison.name: Garrison
garrison.desc: All your outposts are one and a half times tougher. Existing ones too.

bastion.name: Bastion
bastion.desc: Your fort fires its shore gun twice per turn, picking a new target each time.

grapnels.name: Grappling Hooks
grapnels.desc: You take 10% more of a sunk ship price from the wreck — 60% instead of half.

lateen.name: Lateen Sail
lateen.desc: Headwind no longer cuts your movement. Tailwind still helps.

shipyard.name: Streamlined Yard
shipyard.desc: Ships in the shipyard are 10% cheaper.

fishery.name: Fishery
fishery.desc: Every fishing boat in a fishing ground brings 1 more gold per turn.

portRepair.name: Port Repair
portRepair.desc: Instantly restores half of your port hull. A consumable — buy it as many times as your coins allow.
